title: V8 GC versus CLR GC
hook: Both engines are generational tracing collectors. The knobs, the large-object story, and the threading model are where a senior answer splits.

sections.heading: Shared ideas
sections.prose: V8 and the CLR both allocate in a nursery (V8 new space, CLR gen 0), promote survivors to an old generation, mark from roots, and compact or sweep. Both pause mutators for at least some phases. Both struggle when you keep large object graphs from globals or statics. A Redis-sized buffer in Node is a typed array or Buffer; in CLR it is a byte[] that may sit on the LOH. Closures retain graphs in both heaps. That is enough to say they are cousins. It is not enough to say they are the same GC.

snippets.label: Same leak shape, different heap
snippets.explanation: A module-level Map in Node is a root, like a static Dictionary in C#. Neither GC will free entries you still reference.

sections.heading: Where they diverge
sections.prose: The CLR exposes generations 0/1/2, SOH versus LOH, workstation versus server GC, and DATAS. V8 uses scavenge in new space, concurrent marking in old space, and incremental sweeping; operators set --max-old-space-size, not gcServer. V8’s main JS heap is tightly bound to one JS thread; worker threads have their own isolates. The CLR heap is process-wide and many managed threads allocate into it (server GC: one heap per CPU). CLR finalizers run on a dedicated thread; JS FinalizationRegistry callbacks are queued as tasks on the event loop. CLR can compact the LOH on demand; V8’s handling of large objects is internal. When an interviewer asks ‘how is GC different from Node?’, lead with: same reachability idea, different generation layout, different threading, different production knobs, and Dispose/SafeHandle has no exact Node equivalent besides explicit close.

interviewTakeaways: Both: nursery, old generation, roots, mark, leaks via globals.
CLR: gen 0/1/2, LOH, server GC, process-wide heaps, finalizer thread.
V8: isolate per worker, --max-old-space-size, no IDisposable story for native addons other than explicit lifetime.
commonPitfalls: Saying Node has no GC generations.
Claiming server GC exists in V8 under another name.
Equating Isolate.Dispose in Node with CLR Dispose of a bitmap — different layers.
